column1: # Customer alias map — raw customer string  ->  canonical name  ->  why
# The demand signal brief ranks a capability theme primarily by HOW MANY DISTINCT CUSTOMERS
# asked for it. That makes the customer string a ranking dimension, not a label: two spellings
# of one organization silently double its apparent breadth and push a theme up the list.
# Consumed by scripts/demand_signal_core.py::canonical_customer(). The register keeps the RAW
# string on every row — this map only affects grouping and counting, so nothing here rewrites
# history and any mapping can be reversed by editing this file.
# Format: three TAB-separated columns. Lines starting with # are comments. Blank lines ignored.
#   alias<TAB>canonical<TAB>note
# RULE: only map strings that name the SAME buying activity. Different program offices inside
# one agency are different customers — they hold separate money and write separate
# requirements — and collapsing them understates real breadth just as badly as duplicate
# spellings overstate it. When unsure, leave it out; an unmapped name passes through unchanged.
# Run `python scripts/customer-aliases.py --suggest` to see grouping candidates the register
# has accumulated. It proposes; it never edits this file.
AFLCMC
